title: Who is right about the sheet?
scenario: A studio's overnight batch has finished, and the status sheet does not match what people say. You decide how the team should fix its process. The sheet and the events are our own examples, made up for this case. Use the exhibit.
exhibit:
STATUS SHEET (made up for this case):
  id            Copy      Image   Check
  tea-de-9x16   approved  made    FAIL line 3 (Checker, 02:10)
                                  then PASS (Producer, 02:40)
  tea-fr-1x1    approved  made    PASS (Checker, 02:15)

EVENTS (made up for this case):
  02:30  The producer's chat was restarted. It began with an empty memory.
  03:00  The Visual maker pasted all 50 images into the producer's chat to
         pass them on. Two came out changed.
  03:30  The packer role asks for the client's upload password.

questions.prompt: Which rule would have stopped the Producer from overwriting the Checker's result?

options.text: Let every role edit every column, so that mistakes get fixed as fast as they are seen
options.explanation: Many writers cause this problem. A fast overwrite hides the failed line.

options.text: Hide the Check column from the Producer, so that it cannot see any failed lines
options.explanation: The producer should read the result, so that it knows what is left to do. Reading is fine. Writing is the problem.

options.text: Keep the status only in the producer's chat, so that there is only one copy of it
options.explanation: A chat is not a project record. It was restarted and lost its memory.

options.text: Give each column one writer, so only the Checker writes Check and others add a note
options.explanation: Right. This rule is ours: one writer per column. The producer disagrees by adding a note, not by overwriting.

questions.prompt: Two images came out changed when they were pasted through the chat. What does Anthropic's research post suggest?

options.text: Paste the images in smaller groups, so that fewer of them can change on the way
options.explanation: Smaller groups still pass the images through the chat. The loss comes from the passing itself.

options.text: Save each image in the project folder and pass on only a light reference to the file
options.explanation: Right. The Anthropic engineering post says helpers should store their work externally and pass lightweight references back, to avoid the "game of telephone".

options.text: Ask the producer to describe each image in words, and pass on only those descriptions
options.explanation: Words are a summary and lose detail. This is the telephone problem again.

options.text: Ask the producer to check each pasted image against the original before passing it on
options.explanation: This adds a check, but the images still travel through the chat, which is what causes the loss. It also costs more tokens.

questions.prompt: The producer's chat restarted with empty memory. What lets a new producer carry on?

options.text: Ask the model to recall the last run, because it keeps its memory across all new chats
options.explanation: A model sees only what is put in front of it. A new chat does not hold the old one.

options.text: Start again from item 1, because a chat with no memory cannot be trusted at all
options.explanation: This pays again for work that is done. The sheet records what is finished.

options.text: Let the Visual maker say what is done, since it saw all 50 images in the last hour
options.explanation: The visual maker knows its own work only, not checks or sign-off.

options.text: A new producer reads the status sheet and continues with the rows that are not done
options.explanation: Right. The sheet works as a checkpoint. The Anthropic engineering post says restarting from the beginning is expensive, and Anthropic's systems resume from where they were.

questions.prompt: The packer role asks for the client's upload password. Someone suggests adding it to the sheet. What now?

options.text: Add it to the Check column, because the checker is the one who already writes there
options.explanation: The sheet is read by many roles and people. A password does not belong in it.

options.text: Add it for tonight only, since the sheet is private to the team and tonight is the last run
options.explanation: Shared state is read and kept. A password in it can stay there and spread.

options.text: Keep it out of the sheet, and give only the packer role a limited key for uploads
options.explanation: Right. The OpenAI Agents SDK docs warn against putting secrets in context that is stored or sent on. A shared sheet needs the same care. Give the smallest access that works.

options.text: Put it in the brand kit folder, because every role already reads from that place
options.explanation: The brand kit is read by every role. That makes a password there reach every role.
